sections.h2: Which Knox County offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Five phone numbers cover nearly every Knox County tax question, and each leads to the Barbourville courthouse complex at 401 Court Square. The PVA's office sets the value. The sheriff bills and collects. The clerk inherits what goes unpaid, and the county attorney pursues it from there.

Knox County contacts, from the Kentucky Department for Local Government county listing
OfficeUse it forPhone
Property valuation administrator (PVA)Value, exemptions, appeal conferences(606) 546-4113
SheriffPaying the current bill(606) 546-3181
County clerkDeeds, delinquent certificates, filing an appeal(606) 546-3568
County attorneyDelinquent bills and payment talks(606) 546-9515
Fiscal courtGeneral county government(606) 546-6192

Courthouse doors open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:00. Saturday mornings until noon, only the county clerk and circuit clerk offices stay open. To record a deed on a Knox County house, carry it to the clerk on the first floor.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Knox County for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Knox County covers 388 square miles of mountain country in the southeast corner of Kentucky, touching Clay, Bell, Whitley and Laurel counties. Barbourville, the seat, sits where Richland Creek joins the Cumberland River. U.S. 25E runs about 16 miles northwest to Corbin and the same distance southeast to Pineville. Most of Corbin lies in Whitley County, and Artemus and Flat Lick are the other named communities.

The county was cut from Lincoln County on December 19, 1799. Its fifth courthouse opened in 1964. The Wilderness Road crosses it, the first land battle in Kentucky during the Civil War was fought at Barbourville on September 19, 1861, and Dr. Thomas Walker State Park, with a replica of the first house built in Kentucky, is a short drive away. Coal drove the economy for generations, and the county kept more of its jobs and people than most of the coalfield did. Health care, retail and education lead employment today.

The 2020 census counted 30,193 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 29,532, a fall of 2.2 percent. For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau reports:

  • A middle-priced owner-occupied home is worth $118,700.
  • 65.3 percent of the 11,711 households own the place they live in.
  • Rent at the midpoint is $681 a month.
  • The midpoint household income is $32,527.
  • No building permits are recorded for 2025.

At those values even a modest back-tax balance is a meaningful slice of what a sale brings, which is why the payoff figures matter early in a sale.

sections.h2: How does Knox County weather matter to a house?
sections.html:
Barbourville's NOAA normals for 1991 to 2020 show 53.77 inches of precipitation a year, spread over about 143 days with measurable rain or snow. January mornings average 24.6 degrees Fahrenheit, and July afternoons average 87.0. The record low is 22 below zero and the record high is 106.

A wet year-round pattern with hard freezes means a buyer's inspector will look closely at the roof, gutters, crawlspace moisture and plumbing that runs through unheated areas. Sellers who document recent repairs, or who tell a cash buyer plainly what needs work, usually shorten the back-and-forth. The same documentation supports an assessment conference if the PVA's value assumes a house in better shape than yours.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Knox County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the PVA and book a conference; Kentucky will not hear an appeal without one. The roll is open for inspection for thirteen days starting the first Monday in May. After the conference you have until the close of business on the next workday following the last inspection day to file with the county clerk, and the local board takes the case 25 to 35 days later.

Bring proof: photos, bids from contractors, an appraisal, nearby sales. A board given no evidence denies the appeal, and an owner who files but skips the hearing cannot take the case to the Kentucky Claims Commission. The PVA's website says the office assesses at 100 percent of fair market value.

sections.h2: When does Knox County want its tax money?
sections.html:
The assessment-year bill is due by December 31. The Department of Revenue says collection starts October 1 or November 1 in most counties. Because discount and penalty steps differ from county to county, use the dates printed on the bill from the Knox County Sheriff, or call (606) 546-3181.

On April 15 whatever is still owed moves to the county clerk. The person who owned the property on January 1 is personally responsible, and the lien that comes with delinquent taxes lasts eleven years under KRS 134.420, no matter who holds the deed afterward. A buyer inherits that lien with the house, so sellers clear it first.

sections.h2: What does an unpaid Knox County bill turn into?
sections.html:
It becomes a certificate of delinquency with a lien recorded against the parcel. The clerk's website has a delinquent tax lookup and warns that the clerk's own calculation at the time of sale controls.

The state's worked example takes a $1,000 bill to $1,254 at transfer. Paid within five business days it comes to $1,387.79. After the first county attorney letter the total reads $1,611.30, and after a June advertisement $1,659.90.

  • Interest accrues at one percent for each month or part of a month.
  • Two county attorney notices go out, the first at 30 days and the second within 60.
  • A sale takes place 90 to 135 days after the transfer, so mid-July to late August in a regular-schedule county.
  • Notice of the sale is published 30 to 45 days ahead.
  • Someone who buys the certificate at the sale takes over the lien, and the owner then pays that buyer.

sections.h2: Who gets the homestead exemption in Knox County?
sections.html:
An owner aged 65 or over, or classed as totally disabled under a retirement system, can take $49,100 off the home's assessed value for 2025 and 2026. The house must be that person's residence on January 1. Apply to the Knox County PVA by December 31.

Heirs who live elsewhere cannot count on inheriting the break, so ask the PVA what changes after a death.

sections.h2: How are taxes divided when a Knox County house sells?
sections.html:
The bill carries the January 1 owner's name, so a March sale still leaves the seller as taxpayer of record. The settlement statement splits the year and the closing agent pays the sheriff. KRS 382.135(1)(d) requires an in-care-of address on the deed for the bill that year, so supply the buyer's mailing address.

Heirs, owners who fell behind and landlords with an empty rental often ask if a cash buyer can wrap up everything in one closing. The payoff must be known first. Get the current-year number from the sheriff and any older certificate amount from the clerk, then ask the county attorney's office if a payment plan exists, because the title company will want to know.

faqs.q: Who collects Knox County property tax?
faqs.a: The sheriff collects the current bill, at (606) 546-3181. After April 15 the clerk, at (606) 546-3568, takes payment on the delinquent certificate.

faqs.q: What is the first step to dispute a Knox County value?
faqs.a: Book a conference with the PVA at (606) 546-4113. The appeal to the county clerk comes after that, within the window set by the end of the May roll inspection.

faqs.q: What does the homestead exemption take off in Knox County?
faqs.a: $49,100 of assessed value for 2025 and 2026, for owners 65 or older or totally disabled who live in the house. The PVA takes applications through December 31.

faqs.q: Does a Knox County delinquent bill collect interest?
faqs.a: Yes, at one percent per month once it is a certificate at the clerk's office, with commissions and fees added.

faqs.q: Can a house with back taxes in Knox County still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays on the parcel and the payoff is paid from the sale proceeds. Collect written figures from the sheriff and the clerk before choosing a closing date.
